previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and a history of kidney transplant was admitted with worsening bilateral hip pain, cough, and fever. He had missed a dialysis session, presenting with hyperkalemia (K 6.7) that was corrected with emergency dialysis and medical treatment, though he developed transient hypoglycemia afterward. His fever and respiratory symptoms were consistent with a viral upper respiratory infection, supported by negative flu and culture results and a normal chest X-ray. Hip imaging showed progression of avascular necrosis with right femoral head collapse. Trace hematuria was noted, with no signs of infection; urology follow-up was arranged. He improved with supportive care, pain management, and completion of dialysis, and was discharged home with a short course of oxycodone, benzonatate for cough, and plans for outpatient pain and urology evaluation.
